requirement:
The harness MUST expose a `list_files` tool with this interface:

```text
list_files({ path: String = "." }) -> Array<DirectoryEntry>

DirectoryEntry {
    path: String,
    kind: "file" | "directory",
}
```

The tool MUST list the immediate children of the requested directory, returning
project-relative paths where possible and absolute paths for permitted external
files. Its root listing MUST also expose available generated-output directories
and configured external allow paths. The model can list a returned
directory in another call to explore further. A failed listing MUST return an
explanatory tool error unless access was denied, which MUST be handled under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`. Directory listings MUST NOT become evidence inputs.
Listings MUST omit files excluded by {cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`.
In a Git worktree, directories MUST have at least one eligible source
descendant to be listed unless explicitly allowed or discovered as generated
output. Explicitly requesting an excluded path MUST be handled as a denial under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.authoring.file_discovery`. I read the supplied implementation and test items. I did not read the test helpers `dispatch` and `project`, or any items beyond the supplied inputs. I mapped each obligation to code and a test as follows.

- **Tool interface.**
  - `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[definitions]` declares `list_files` with an optional `path` that defaults to `.`.
  - `fn[list_files]` returns entries shaped `{path, kind}`, where `kind` is `file` or `directory`.
  - `fn[optional_path]` applies the default.
  - `fn[check_keys]` rejects unknown arguments.
  - `fn[dispatch_paged]` routes the call.
  - `mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` asserts the exact `[{"path":"src/lib.rs","kind":"file"}]` result.
- **Immediate children and path form.**
  - `fn[list_files]` iterates `fs::read_dir` of the requested directory.
  - `fn[relative_path]` returns a project-relative path, or the absolute path when the entry is outside the root.
  - Tests that list children: `fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` and `fn[git_tools_allow_staged_and_dirty_sources_but_hide_untracked_files]`.
  - Test that checks an absolute path for an external allow path: `fn[allowed_ignored_and_external_sources_are_discoverable_but_disallowed_descendants_are_not]`.
- **Root listing exposes generated-output directories and external allow paths.**
  - When the directory is the root, `fn[list_files]` adds every entry from `SourceAccess::extra_roots`, which chains `policy.allow` and the discovered `generated` directories.
  - `fn[allowed_ignored_and_external_sources_are_discoverable_but_disallowed_descendants_are_not]` asserts that `generated` and the external directory appear.
  - `fn[cargo_output_is_discovered_and_read_without_building_or_allowing_other_target_files]` asserts that `target/debug/build/fixture-hash/out` appears.
- **Failed listing returns an explanatory tool error.**
  - `fn[list_files]` wraps `read_dir` failures in a "cannot list …" message.
  - `fn[optional_path]` and `fn[check_keys]` produce errors for malformed arguments.
  - `fn[failed_listings_return_explanatory_tool_errors]` covers a missing path, a file path, a non-string path and an extra argument. It asserts none is a `PermissionDenied`.
  - Access denial is handled by `read_denial`, which this subject cites and does not reassess.
- **Listings are not evidence inputs.** `ToolDelivery.inputs` is empty for listings. `fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` asserts `listing.inputs.is_empty()`.
- **Excluded files omitted.**
  - `fn[list_files]` skips any entry for which `SourceAccess::path` errors.
  - That check covers `evidence/` and its symlink aliases (`fn[generated_evidence_path]`), outside-project symlinks, untracked files and disallowed paths.
  - Tests: `fn[generated_evidence_is_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery]`, `fn[outside_symlinks_are_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery]`, `fn[git_tools_allow_staged_and_dirty_sources_but_hide_untracked_files]`, `fn[git_symlink_reads_require_both_the_alias_and_target_to_be_tracked]`, and the disallow checks in `fn[cargo_output_is_discovered_and_read_without_building_or_allowing_other_target_files]`.
- **Git worktree: a directory needs an eligible source descendant.**
  - In `SourceAccess::path`, `fn[has_source_under]` is applied when a tracked index exists and the target is a directory.
  - Allowed and generated paths return earlier, so the "unless explicitly allowed or discovered as generated output" exception holds.
  - `fn[git_tools_allow_staged_and_dirty_sources_but_hide_untracked_files]` shows `untracked-dir` is absent from the root listing.
- **Explicitly requesting an excluded path is handled as a denial.**
  - `SourceAccess::path` returns `PermissionDenied` errors for these cases.
  - `fn[converse]` returns the error to the model as a tool error and continues. Its comment carries the `read_denial` reference.
  - Tests: `fn[generated_evidence_is_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery]`, `fn[git_tools_allow_staged_and_dirty_sources_but_hide_untracked_files]`, `fn[allowed_ignored_and_external_sources_are_discoverable_but_disallowed_descendants_are_not]`, `fn[cargo_output_is_discovered_and_read_without_building_or_allowing_other_target_files]`, and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[explicit_untracked_reads_return_an_untracked_error_and_the_assessment_continues]`.

All helpers (`resolve`, `recoverable_outside_request`, `project_path`) are reachable from the marked items. All the tests named above carry `{test}` references to the subject. I saw no unspecified extra behavior.

When source-access policy denies a path that a model tool call names
explicitly, the harness MUST return a tool error naming the path and the reason
it cannot be read, add no evidence input, and continue the assessment.
Discovery and search MUST leave denied candidates out of their entries,
reporting untracked ones under {cite}`requirements.authoring.not_listed`. Malformed tool
arguments and ordinary read failures MUST also return explanatory tool errors.
:::{req} source_tools
The harness MUST expose a `habeas` tool accepting exactly one of these request
forms. Each form MUST correspond to one existing evidence-input kind:
| Request fields | Evidence input returned | Definition |
| `file: String`, `line_start: Integer`, optional `line_end: Integer` | Outline inputs for the innermost outline nodes covering the range | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `file: String`, `item: String` | Outline input | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `requirements: String` | Requirements input, including its matching names | {cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs` |
| `definition: String` | Definition input | {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs` |
Selector arguments MUST use the syntax defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Reads MUST use the current
project working tree, including unstaged changes to tracked files and staged new
files. By default, source inputs MUST stay within the project root after
resolving symlinks; in a Git worktree, both the requested file and its resolved
target MUST be present in the Git index. Projects outside Git MUST use the same
containment rules without requiring an index. Failure to read an existing
repository's index MUST be reported as an error.
The project-root `evidence/` directory MUST be excluded from model reads by
default, including symlink aliases. Every source the harness supplies to the
model MUST be redacted under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. Generated build outputs MUST follow
{cite}`requirements.authoring.generated_inputs`. Workspace path overrides MUST
follow {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`, including explicit
permission for otherwise excluded inputs. A denied mandatory input MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`, and a denied model
read MUST return a tool error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
Line numbers are only a way to request sources; recorded evidence MUST identify
sources by outline selector and structural hash, never by line number. Request
line numbers MUST be one-based and inclusive, and omitting `line_end` MUST read
through EOF. A line-range request MUST be resolved to the innermost outline
nodes covering the requested lines, which are `line` nodes in a file using the
plain-text profile; the result MUST show the model each node's selector and
source text, without line numbers, and the harness MUST record those nodes as
outline inputs. The model-facing tool description MUST include the argument conventions
from the cited requirements, including outline selector syntax, definition
selections, and full definition names, with a short request example for each form.
A successful call MUST return the requested evidence input, populated by the
harness with the selected source text, using the existing evidence schema.
